A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extent of CAD in patients presenting with non‐ST elevation ACS is a predictor of long term outcome, and that a high risk score is associated with a higher rate of angiographic extent of disease and a higher rate of adverse events.
we identified a group of patients with non-ST elevation ACS who had high risk angiographic findings and were at increased risk of major adverse cardiac events.
we have shown that patients with NSTE-ACS and high-risk findings on angiography have worse outcomes than patients with NSTE -ACS with low-risk angiographic findings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extent of CAD in NSTE‐ACS is associated with increased mortality and that this association is stronger in patients with a history of myocardial infarction.
the extent of CAD and the presence of severe CAD are associated with adverse prognosis.
the extent of coronary atherosclerosis is associated with the presence of diabetes mellitus and with the presence of atherosclerotic plaques in the coronary arteries.
